title: Existence of an ample module lifts from the reduction in characteristic p
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $X$ a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning that $X$ has a finite affine open covering by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume $p\mathcal O_X=0$, meaning that $p\cdot1=0$ in every local ring. Let $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ be its reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. If $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ admits an absolutely ample invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then $X$ admits an absolutely ample invertible module. No lift of a specified module is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0BD4, proposition-push-down-ample, case (3), applied to the reduction closed immersion; proof uses lemma-Frobenius-gives-norm-for-reduction and lemma-norm-ample.

proof.text: Put $Y=X_{\mathrm{red}}$ and let $i:Y\to X$ be the reduction immersion. By [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], $i$ is a closed immersion and the identity on underlying points; in particular it is surjective with singleton fibres. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Apply [lem-sfb-reduction-frobenius-sheaf-norm] to the given Noetherian $X$ and prime $p$: obtain $e\geq1$ and maps $\nu_V$ satisfying all norm conditions, of degree $d=p^e\geq1$.

Choose an ample invertible module $M$ on $Y$ from the hypothesis. Since $i$ is finite surjective and the maps $\nu_V$ preserve multiplication and $1$, commute with restriction, have the scalar-power property and satisfy residue-field vanishing, [lem-sfb-finite-norm-invertible-sections] gives an invertible module $N$ on $X$. Fix this single $N$; it provides the asserted norm sections for every positive tensor power and every global section of that power of $M$.

Fix $x\in X$ and an affine open neighbourhood $V$ of $x$. The fibre $E=i^{-1}(\{x\})$ is a singleton and lies in the open $i^{-1}V$. By [lem-sc-ample-finite-principal-affine], applied on $Y$ to $M,E,i^{-1}V$, choose $n>0$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$ with $E\subseteq Y_s\subseteq i^{-1}V$.

By [lem-sfb-finite-norm-invertible-sections] there is $t\in\Gamma(X,N^{\otimes n})$ with $X_t=\{z:i^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq Y_s\}$. Thus $x\in X_t$. If $z\in X_t$, surjectivity of $i$ gives a point $y$ above $z$, and then $y\in Y_s\subseteq i^{-1}V$, whence $z\in V$. Therefore $X_t\subseteq V$, and $X_t=V\cap X_t$ is affine by [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open], applied to $N,n,t,V$.

Ampleness of $M$ makes $Y$ quasi-compact by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Pull any open cover of $X$ back to $Y$, choose a finite subcover, and use surjectivity of $i$ to see that the corresponding finite family covers $X$. Thus $X$ is quasi-compact. The preceding construction supplies at every $x\in X$ an affine nonvanishing locus of a section of a positive power of $N$ containing $x$. These are exactly the two conditions of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], so $N$ is ample. This constructs some ample module, without claiming to lift $M$.

tool_uses.why: The general finiteness of a closed immersion supplies finiteness of the reduction immersion.
The general ample-section lemma supplies a section around the singleton fibre inside the inverse image of an affine neighbourhood.
The general affine-intersection lemma proves that the descended norm section has affine nonvanishing open.
